On the basis of the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.2471 of 2024 dated 10.05.2024 notice was issued upon the respondent No.2 by both ways i.e. under ordinary process as well as registered cover with A/D and from the service report, it is found that the notice through Courts as well as under registered post with A/D was received by the respondent No.2.
However, she has not chosen to appear to contest the instant writ petition.

Therefore, I have no other alternative but to take up the hearing of the writ petition in presence of Mr. Ashish Giri, learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners and Mr. Manish Kumar, learned Advocate on behalf of the State.

3. It would not be out of list to mention at the outset that on 27.02.2024 the instant writ petition was disposed of, quashing the F.I.R. in connection with Hawaiadda P.S. sentences.text: However, by virtue of the solemn order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Criminal Appeal No.2471 of 2024, the aforesaid order was set aside on the ground that the respondent No.2 was not heard and this Court was directed to rehear and dispose of the above- mentioned writ petition after service of notice upon the respondent No.2.
Now, respondent No.2 being served, there is no impediment to hear out the instant writ petition.
4. The factual aspect of the matter is not in dispute.

The petitioners are the elder brother-in-law,
wife of the said elder brother-in-law and their two children, who were made accused in connection with Hawaiadda P.S. Case No.15 of 2021 under Sections 341, 323, 504, 498A, 34 of the Indian Penal Patna High Court CR.
WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

5. The above-named petitioners filed the instant writ petition praying for issuance of writ in the nature of certiorari quashing the aforementioned F.I.R. lodged against them as well as the Charge Sheet No.183/2022 dated 19.07.2022.
6.

The de facto complainant/respondent No.2 is the married wife of one Dr. Parmanand Parmhansh,
whose marriage was solemnized on 19.04.2015.

Previously the respondent No.2 filed a complaint in a Jurisdictional Court, which was registered as Complaint Case No.3985(C) of 2019 under Sections 498A, 323, 506 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence vide order dated 07.01.2020 against the petitioners and the husband of the complainant, under Section 498A/323 of the I.P.C.
The said complaint case is still pending.

However, further proceeding of the complaint case was stayed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Cr. Misc. No.67024 of 2023 vide order dated 01.11.2023.
7.

Be that as it may during the pendency of the said complaint case, Hawaiadda P.S. Case No.15 of 2021 was registered on the basis of an F.I.R. filed by the respondent No.2, alleging, inter-alia, that after her marriage with Dr. Parmanand Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1629 of 2023(3)
dt.06-12-2024 Parmhansh, the accused persons used to instigate her, abused her with filthy language and used to assault her.
They also demanded money from her and since the father of the informant was retired Government employee, it was not possible to her father to satisfy the demand of the petitioners.
8. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has reiterated what he submitted during the disposal of the instant writ petition previously.
9. It is contended by him that the petitioners and the informant reside separately in separate houses.

The house property of the parties has been partitioned amongst the co- sharers and there was no occasion to instigate the respondent No.2 or to assault her or to make any demand of money,
because the petitioners had no scope to visit the house of the respondent No.2 where she resides separately.

It is also contended by him that the entire allegation made by the Respondent No.2 was on the face value and not a single documentary evidence has been filed in support of her allegation.

sentences.text: It is alleged that she was assaulted by the petitioners but not a scrap of medical documents was placed by her before the Investigating Officer.
She did not specifically state the date and time of the alleged incident when she was instigated and abused by the petitioners.
Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 10.

11. Thus, all sorts of cruelty in the form of abuse or assault does not come within the meaning of Section 498A of I.P.C., Cruelty is synonymous to willful harassment, when such harassment was for extorting valuable property from the married women or her relatives.

Secondly, cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A I.P.C. extends to such degree of mentally and physically torture that leads the married women to commit suicide or to cause grave injury of her life, lien or health.

These Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 ingredients of section 498A I.P.C. is missing in the F.I.R. filed by respondent No.2.
12.
The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners refers to a recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Abhishek Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in (2023) SCC Online SC 1083.

entities.text: Abhishek Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in (2023) SCC Online SC 1083
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above-mentioned report, the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the factual backdrop came to discuss the scope of Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. to quash the F.I.R. even when a charge-sheet is filed by the police.

13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court relies on the decision in V. Ravi Kumar Vs. State, represented by Inspector of Police, District Crime Branch, Salem, Tamil Nadu, reported in (2019) 14 SCC 568 to hold that when an accused seeks quashing of the F.I.R., invoking the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court, it is wholly impermissible for the High Court to enter into the factual arena to adjudge the correctness of the allegations in the complaint.

State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal No.330 of 2021, decided on 13.04.2021) and observed that the power of quashing should be exercised sparingly, with circumspection and in the rarest of rare cases, such standard not being confused Patna High Court CR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. In Neelu Chopra Vs. Bharti, reported in (2009) 10 SCC 184, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that mere mention of statutory provisions and the language thereof, for lodging a complaint, is not the 'be all and end all' of the matter, as what is required to be brought to the notice of the Court is the particulars of the offence committed by each and every accused and the role played by each and every accused in the commission of that offence.

entities.text: Neelu Chopra Vs. Bharti, reported in (2009) 10 SCC 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Para-16 of the aforementioned judgment,
Abhishek (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as follows :-
"16.

Of more recent origin is the decision of this Court in Mahmood Ali v. State of U.P. (Criminal Appeal No. 2341 of 2023, decided on 08.08.2023) on the legal principles applicable apropos Section 482 Cr.P.C. Therein, it was observed that when an accused comes before the High Court, invoking either the inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. or the extraordinary Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution, to get the FIR or the criminal proceedings quashed, essentially on the ground that such proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive of wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances, the High Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.

entities.text: Mahmood Ali v. State of U.P. (Criminal Appeal No. 2341 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further observed that it will not be enough for the Court to look into the averments made in the FIR/complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not as, in frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above the averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection, to try and read between the lines."
16.
Subsequent to the said observation the Hon'ble Supreme Court relied on the decision of Bhajan Lal with approval.
The salient points, where an F.I.R. may be quashed is delineated in Para-10 of the judgment, which was set aside by this Court.
This Court does not think reiterations of Bhajan Lals case because the seven golden points regarding quashing of F.I.R. is imprinted in the heads and hearts of the judges.

17. Again in Payal Sharma Vs. State of Punjab (Criminal Appeal No.--- of 2024 arising out of SLP (CRL) Patna High Court CR. WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 No.3995/2022 decided on 26.11.2024, the Hon'ble Supreme Court discussed the previous judgments of the Apex Court in Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667, Geeta Mehrotra Vs. Sate of Uttar Pradesh, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 and Umesh Kumar Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, reported in (2013) 10 SCC 591 and quashed the F.I.R. and charge sheet alleging offence under Section 498A I.P.C. and other offences.
18.

On careful perusal of the written complaint submitted by the respondent No.2 in the police station, it is ascertained that respondent No.2 has lodged that after her marriage, the petitioners Hira Lal Hans @ Hira Lal Mahto vs The State Of Bihar Through The Principal ... on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25708724/
4 being the relatives of her husband used to instigate her husband to assault her on demand of a sum of Rs.5,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Her father being a retired government employee could not satisfy the said demand.
The F.I.R. does not disclose any date or time of the alleged incident.
It also does not disclose the specific role of the petitioners.
When the illegal claim of dowry was made has not been described.

Under such omnibus and general allegation, can a criminal trial proceed 'my considered reply will be in negative'.
19.
In view of such circumstances and discussions made herein-above, and also relying the law laid down by the Patna High Court CR.
WJC No.1629 of 2023(3) dt.06-12-2024 Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above mentioned cases, this Court is of the view that the instant writ petition is liable to be allowed.
20. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed on contest against the State-respondents and ex-parte against the respondent No.2.
The Hawaiadda P.S. Case No.15 of 2021 and charge sheet be quashed.
21. Let, a copy of this order be sent to the learned Court below for recording discharge of the petitioners forthwith.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) mdrashid/-
